comparator.name: Plant Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Current BPW Plant Production and Ecology pathway:105 compulsory taught +3 conditional mathematics/statistics +24 specialisation +18 thesis +30 genuinely open credits =180. First-year compulsory57 plus conditional3 =60; B2 common48 plus route12 =60; B3 route12 plus thesis18 plus open30 =60. The separately credited Introduction8, Ecology3 and Crop Recognition2 have distinct current course identities/content/assessments; their coordinated first-period scheduling is not a parent/child credit duplication. Three safety courses carry zero credits. MAT14803 is prescribed for Mathematics A preparation, not chosen by source-order tie-break; MAT15303 applies to Mathematics B. The selected introduction is in B1 period2 first-half morning before Statistics2 in the second half; school statistics provides its stated preparation, while later Analysis/Linear Algebra follow the introduction. Complete all132 prescribed taught credits and obtain coordinator permission before YPS82318. Current module/handbook rules are sufficient; an unavailable historical guide is not used to supply missing requirements. No named minor, extra safety/reflection credit or second specialisation is invented.

components.name: Introduction Plant Sciences
components.note: An 8-credit introduction with disciplinary case studies, field/lab activity and academic development. The written tests and group report each require a passing mark; the personal development plan and information-literacy work must also pass. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety are additional zero-credit requirements.

components.name: Crop Recognition
components.note: A separate 2-credit course in identifying crop species and products. Attendance, workbook/excursion and longitudinal assignments must be completed, and the recognition test must pass; this is distinct from the introductory course.

components.name: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Plant Sciences in Practice
components.note: Includes ecological field data, a group-designed greenhouse experiment, presentations, company/institution visits and interviews with three plant-science professionals. Reflection must pass; presentations require a sufficient combined result and minimum marks for their components.

components.name: Biology and Management of Plant Pests and Diseases
Resilience in Plant Sciences: Integrated Research from Molecules to Agro-Ecosystems
components.note: A 12-credit integrated research course. Students conduct a project in pairs, write an individual scientific paper, and work across molecular-to-agroecosystem perspectives on a resilience case. The paper and group case each require a passing mark; individual reflection must also pass.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.note: The 3-credit choice depends on prior mathematics: this example takes Mathematics Applied: Introduction for Mathematics A preparation. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1. Statistics 2 assumes active school statistics or Statistics 1.

components.name: Agricultural Ecosystems - Linking Ecology, Agronomy & Rural Realities
Physiology and Development of Plants in Agriculture
BSc Thesis Plant Sciences
components.note: Required 18-credit individual plant-science research project: proposal, experiments, data analysis, written report, oral presentation, discussion and reflection/future study plan. Entry requires coordinator permission and at least 102 prescribed credits, including all first-year credits. This example completes all 132 prescribed taught credits before the thesis; permission remains a requirement.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: Thirty open credits remain for a minor and/or individual electives. Seagriculture, Experimental Plant Sciences and Resilient Crops are optional minors, not additional compulsory specialisations; no particular minor is assumed.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All formal prerequisites occur in earlier semesters and every assigned term is planned. Biological and chemical gateways precede later cellular/biochemical/laboratory and environmental work. Cell Biology precedes molecular pathology/genetics in the molecular route; basic statistics/design precedes advanced analysis. Soil science and ecology support farming applications, and introductory economics/sociology precede later policy/qualitative work where feasible. No extra hard prerequisites invented.

alternativeSelection.assessment: First reconstruct the strongest biological/ecological response using actual cell/biochemical, biodiversity, farming, soil/water and quantitative content, rather than human physiology or clinical immunity. Then accept a distinct molecular/laboratory/computational response after removing the former neuroscience organising weight. Then accept an ecological farming/resource-policy response: six courses apart from the closest route, with actual farming/environmental science and specific economic/qualitative/policy methods. Pairwise differences are8/6/13 courses,60/45/97.5EC. The organising priorities precede selection and were checked for programme-level response, not coherence alone. Stop at three; remaining optional-minor directions are not automatically extra specialisations. Major plant physiology, crop recognition/reproduction/breeding, pest management and specialist greenhouse/field/research depth remain explicit limits.

notes.text: WUR builds sustained expertise in plant structure and physiology, crop recognition and reproduction, breeding, pests and diseases, cultivation, and plant-specific field, greenhouse and experimental research. These UCR programmes offer related biological, ecological, molecular, environmental and analytical perspectives, with substantial gaps in that specialist plant-science sequence.

audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s Dutch-taught Plant Sciences bachelor studies how plants function and interact with their environment, from cells and genes to crops and agroecosystems. It combines biological research with applications to food production, health, renewable resources and environmental resilience.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme connects biological mechanisms with ecology, farming and soil-environment study. The second emphasises molecular, laboratory and computational methods; the third focuses on sustainable farming and resource-policy decisions. WUR provides substantially more plant physiology, crop recognition, breeding, pest management and specialist greenhouse/field research. Its 18-credit thesis is required; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.
